subject.title: fix: reject malformed UTF-8 in provider HTTP text responses

question: Should malformed bytes in non-JSON provider error bodies fail the request with a decode exception, or should OpenClaw preserve the original provider failure with a safe fallback diagnostic?
rationale: The PR changes an error-reporting compatibility boundary rather than only tightening JSON parsing, and the intended user-visible failure mode needs an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Preserve error fallback
options.body: Keep lossy text decoding or catch the decode failure so callers retain the provider HTTP status and diagnostic context.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed text decoding
options.body: Accept decode exceptions for malformed text responses, but document the compatibility change and prove all provider error callers surface useful context.

recommendation.title: Preserve error fallback
recommendation.body: Keep lossy text decoding or catch the decode failure so callers retain the provider HTTP status and diagnostic context.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence adjacent routing candidate for the provider/agents error boundary.
